newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends higher on wobbly peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends higher on wobbly peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 130 basis points at 20.30 percent on what traders said was speculation spurred by a zigzagging foreign exchange market.
"If any one for any reason begins to acquire dolalr positions, then the money market becomes volatile," a fixed-income analyst said.
"Forex volatility was forced and that led to speculative upside pressure on secondary rates," he added.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 1.7 centavos at 7.9600/7.9630 per dollar.
Earlier in the session, Banco de Mexico decided to break the dominant trend thus far this year and inject liquidity into the market.
Dealers said the move was designed to offset upside pressure on rates, but had little impact.

Overnight rates on bank paper closed up 50 basis points at 19.75 percent. Liquidity of 80 million pesos was due to
return to the system on Monday from prior central bank participation.
